mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressures, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI increases above 2% do not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the unemployment rate increase does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the past 2 months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the decline in housing starts does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 2 months signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the increase in industrial production does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the past month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the decrease in nonfarm payrolls does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 1% over the past 2 months, it signals a shift from investment to consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and INDPRO decrease > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between RSAFS and INDPRO does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.5% over the past month, it signals a tightening monetary policy coupled with labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown indicators.
